text: Watch how you practice your righteousness — not to be watched by others, or you lose the reward waiting with your Father.
When you give to someone in need, don't make a show of it like the show-offs do in the meeting halls and streets; they've already spent their reward.
When you give, keep it quiet enough that even your other hand barely knows,
so the gift stays hidden — and your Father, who watches what's hidden, will repay you.
And when you pray, don't be like the show-offs, loving to stand where crowds will see them pray; they've already spent their reward.
Instead, go into a private room, shut the door, and pray to your Father who is there in secret; he'll repay you.
And don't babble on with empty repetition like the outsiders do, thinking a pile of words gets them heard.
Don't copy them — your Father already knows what you need before you ask.
So pray along these lines: Our Father in the heavens, may your name be treated as holy.
May your kingdom arrive, your will be carried out, here on earth the same as in heaven.
Give us the food we need for today.
Forgive us what we owe, in the same way we forgive those who owe us.
Don't lead us into testing, but keep us safe from the evil one.
Because if you forgive others their wrongs, your heavenly Father will forgive yours too.
But if you refuse to forgive others, your Father won't forgive your wrongs either.
When you fast, don't put on a gloomy face like the show-offs, who twist their expressions so everyone notices their fasting; they've already spent their reward.
Instead, when you fast, wash your face and comb your hair,
so no one but your Father, who sees what's hidden, knows you're fasting — and he'll repay you.
Don't pile up treasure here on earth, where insects and decay ruin it and burglars break in and steal it.
Pile up treasure in heaven instead, where nothing ruins it and no thief can reach it.
Because wherever your treasure sits, that's where your heart will follow.
The eye is like a lamp for the body — if your eye is clear, your whole body is full of light.
But if your eye is clouded, your whole body fills with darkness; and if the light in you is actually darkness, how deep that darkness is.
No one can be a slave to two masters at once — you'll end up loving one and hating the other, or loyal to one and dismissive of the other. You cannot serve both God and riches.
So I'm telling you: don't be anxious about your life — what you'll eat or drink, or what you'll wear. Isn't life worth more than food, and the body more than clothing?
Look at the birds overhead — they don't plant, harvest, or store grain in barns, yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren't you worth far more than birds?
And which of you, by fretting, can add even a single hour to your life?
And why worry about clothing? Study the wildflowers growing in the fields — they don't labor or weave,
yet I tell you, not even Solomon in his full splendor was dressed as beautifully as one of these.
If God dresses the grass of the field so well — grass that's here today and burned in a fire tomorrow — won't he do far more for you, you who trust so little?
So don't be anxious, asking, 'What will we eat?' or 'What will we drink?' or 'What will we wear?'
Those are the things people without faith chase after; your heavenly Father already knows you need all of them.
Put his kingdom and his righteousness first, and all these other things will be provided for you as well.
So don't worry about tomorrow — tomorrow will bring its own worries. Each day already has enough trouble of its own.
